```text
269	function activityTimestampMs(timestamp: string) {
270	  const value = new Date(timestamp).getTime();
271	  return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0;
272	}
273	
274	/**
275	 * Position the `messages`-table rows the loaded stream window has no entry for.
276	 *
277	 * The stream's `seq` is the only ordering authority in this transcript, and a
278	 * database row carries none, so it has to borrow one from the entry it
279	 * precedes. The whole batch is placed in one pass: placing each row on its own
280	 * gave every row that anchored to the same entry the identical fractional seq,
281	 * so a window that postdated several messages stacked all of them into a
282	 * single block instead of leaving them in send order.
283	 *
284	 * Each anchor's rows are spread across the open interval `(anchor - 1, anchor)`,
285	 * which is empty of real entries by construction — integer seqs are unique.
286	 */
287	function assignFallbackUserMessageSeqs(
288	  messages: ReadonlyArray<TerminalUserMessage>,
289	  entries: WorkerEntry[],
290	): Map<string, number> {
291	  const placements = new Map<string, number>();
292	  const orderedEntries = entries
293	    .filter((entry) => typeof entry.seq === "number")
294	    .sort((left, right) => left.seq - right.seq);
295	  const latestSeq = orderedEntries.at(-1)?.seq;
296	  if (typeof latestSeq !== "number") {
297	    return placements;
298	  }
299	
300	  const byAnchor = new Map<number, TerminalUserMessage[]>();
301	  for (const message of messages) {
302	    const messageTime = activityTimestampMs(message.createdAt);
303	    const nextEntry = orderedEntries.find((entry) => activityTimestampMs(entry.timestamp) >= messageTime);
304	    // No entry is newer than the message: it belongs after everything loaded.
305	    const anchor = nextEntry ? nextEntry.seq : latestSeq + 1;
306	    const bucket = byAnchor.get(anchor);
307	    if (bucket) {
308	      bucket.push(message);
309	    } else {
310	      byAnchor.set(anchor, [message]);
311	    }
312	  }
313	
314	  for (const [anchor, bucket] of byAnchor) {
315	    const ordered = [...bucket].sort((left, right) => (
316	      activityTimestampMs(left.createdAt) - activityTimestampMs(right.createdAt)
317	      || left.id.localeCompare(right.id)
318	    ));
319	    const step = 1 / (ordered.length + 1);
320	    ordered.forEach((message, index) => {
321	      placements.set(message.id, anchor - 1 + step * (index + 1));
322	    });
323	  }
324	  return placements;
325	}
326	
327	function normalizeUserMessageText(text: string | null | undefined) {
328	  return (text ?? "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
329	}
330	
331	function timestampDistanceMs(left: string | null | undefined, right: string | null | undefined) {
332	  const leftTime = left ? new Date(left).getTime() : Number.NaN;
333	  const rightTime = right ? new Date(right).getTime() : Number.NaN;
334	  if (!Number.isFinite(leftTime) || !Number.isFinite(rightTime)) {
335	    return Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
336	  }
337	  return Math.abs(leftTime - rightTime);
338	}
339	
340	function workerEntryMatchesUserMessage(entry: WorkerEntry, message: TerminalUserMessage) {
341	  if (entry.type !== "user_input") {
342	    return false;
343	  }
344	  if (entry.id === message.id) {
345	    return true;
346	  }
347	  return normalizeUserMessageText(entry.text) === normalizeUserMessageText(message.content)
348	    && timestampDistanceMs(entry.timestamp, message.createdAt) <= 5_000;
349	}

351	function activityKindOrder(activity: TerminalActivityItem) {
352	  switch (activity.kind) {
353	    case "user_message":
354	      return 0;
355	    case "pending_assistant":
356	      return 1;
357	    case "thinking":
358	    case "work_summary":
359	      return 2;
360	    case "tool":
361	    case "tool_group":
362	      return 3;
363	    case "permission":
364	      return 4;
365	    case "message":
366	      return 5;
367	    default:
368	      return 6;
369	  }
370	}

372	/**
373	 * Keep one activity item per message id: the last delivery wins. Items without
374	 * a messageId (or without a duplicate) pass through untouched, and the survivor
375	 * keeps the position of the newest copy so a re-delivered message renders where
376	 * it was actually sent again, not where it was originally sent.
377	 */
378	function dedupeUserActivityByMessageId<T extends TerminalActivityItemWithOrder>(items: T[]): T[] {
379	  // Last occurrence wins: the entries feeding this list arrive oldest-first
380	  // (the transcript is sorted server-side), so the final copy of a message id
381	  // is its most recent delivery. `streamSeq` cannot break the tie — it is
382	  // per-worker, and the re-delivery starts a new worker's numbering.
383	  const lastIndexByMessageId = new Map<string, number>();
384	  items.forEach((item, index) => {
385	    if (item.kind === "user_message") {
386	      lastIndexByMessageId.set(item.messageId, index);
387	    }
388	  });
389	
390	  return items.filter((item, index) => (
391	    item.kind !== "user_message" || lastIndexByMessageId.get(item.messageId) === index
392	  ));
393	}
394	
395	function activityStreamSeq(
396	  activity: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder,
397	  seqByActivityId: Map<string, number>,
398	): number | null {
399	  if (typeof activity.streamSeq === "number") {
400	    return activity.streamSeq;
401	  }
402	  if (activity.kind === "tool_group") {
403	    const seqs = activity.tools
404	      .map((tool) => seqByActivityId.get(tool.id))
405	      .filter((seq): seq is number => typeof seq === "number");
406	    return seqs.length > 0 ? Math.min(...seqs) : null;
407	  }
408	  if (activity.id.startsWith("message-fragment-run:")) {
409	    const parts = activity.id.split(":");
410	    const firstId = parts[1];
411	    if (firstId) {
412	      return seqByActivityId.get(firstId) ?? null;
413	    }
414	  }
415	  return seqByActivityId.get(activity.id) ?? null;
416	}
417	
418	/**
419	 * Give every activity item one scalar order key, resolved before any
420	 * comparison happens.
421	 *
422	 * The comparator used to decide per *pair* whether seq or timestamp applied,
423	 * falling back to timestamp whenever either side had no seq. That is not a
424	 * total order: with items A(seq 1, late), B(no seq, mid) and C(seq 5, early),
425	 * A sorts before C by seq, C before B by timestamp, and B before A by
426	 * timestamp — a cycle, so the result depended on which pairs `sort` happened
427	 * to compare. Items that carry a seq keep it; items that do not borrow one
428	 * from the seq-carrying item they precede, the same rule fallback user
429	 * messages are placed by, so the whole list is ordered by a single quantity.
430	 */
431	function assignActivityOrderKeys(
432	  items: ReadonlyArray<TerminalActivityItemWithOrder>,
433	  seqByActivityId: Map<string, number>,
434	): Map<string, number> {
435	  const resolved = items.map((item) => ({ item, seq: activityStreamSeq(item, seqByActivityId) }));
436	  const anchors = resolved
437	    .filter((candidate): candidate is { item: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder; seq: number } => (
438	      candidate.seq !== null
439	    ))
440	    .sort((left, right) => left.seq - right.seq);
441	
442	  const orderKeys = new Map<string, number>();
443	  for (const { item, seq } of resolved) {
444	    if (seq !== null) {
445	      orderKeys.set(item.id, seq);
446	    }
447	  }
448	  if (anchors.length === 0) {
449	    // Nothing carries a seq (legacy `agent` rendering): timestamps order the
450	    // list on their own.
451	    for (const { item } of resolved) {
452	      orderKeys.set(item.id, activityTimestampMs(item.timestamp));
453	    }
454	    return orderKeys;
455	  }
456	
457	  const latestAnchorSeq = anchors.at(-1)!.seq;
458	  const byAnchor = new Map<number, TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[]>();
459	  for (const { item, seq } of resolved) {
460	    if (seq !== null) {
461	      continue;
462	    }
463	    const itemTime = activityTimestampMs(item.timestamp);
464	    const nextAnchor = anchors.find((anchor) => activityTimestampMs(anchor.item.timestamp) >= itemTime);
465	    const anchorSeq = nextAnchor ? nextAnchor.seq : latestAnchorSeq + 1;
466	    const bucket = byAnchor.get(anchorSeq);
467	    if (bucket) {
468	      bucket.push(item);
469	    } else {
470	      byAnchor.set(anchorSeq, [item]);
471	    }
472	  }
473	
474	  for (const [anchorSeq, bucket] of byAnchor) {
475	    const ordered = [...bucket].sort((left, right) => (
476	      activityTimestampMs(left.timestamp) - activityTimestampMs(right.timestamp)
477	      || left.id.localeCompare(right.id)
478	    ));
479	    const step = 1 / (ordered.length + 1);
480	    ordered.forEach((item, index) => {
481	      orderKeys.set(item.id, anchorSeq - 1 + step * (index + 1));
482	    });
483	  }
484	  return orderKeys;
485	}

495	function formatThoughtDuration(durationMs: number | undefined) {
496	  if (durationMs == null) {
497	    return null;
498	  }
499	
500	  const totalSeconds = Math.round(durationMs / 1000);
501	  if (totalSeconds < 1) {
502	    return null;
503	  }
504	  if (totalSeconds < 60) {
505	    return `${totalSeconds}s`;
506	  }
507	
508	  const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);
509	  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;
510	  return seconds > 0 ? `${minutes}m ${seconds}s` : `${minutes}m`;
511	}
512	
513	function formatThoughtLabel(activity: Extract<AgentActivityItem, { kind: "thinking" }>) {
514	  if (activity.inProgress) {
515	    return "Thinking";
516	  }
517	
518	  const duration = formatThoughtDuration(activity.durationMs);
519	  return duration ? `Thought for ${duration}` : "Thought";
520	}
521	
522	function formatWorkDuration(durationMs: number): string {
523	  const totalSeconds = Math.max(1, Math.round(durationMs / 1000));
524	  const hours = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 3600);
525	  const minutes = Math.floor((totalSeconds % 3600) / 60);
526	  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;
527	  const parts: string[] = [];
528	  if (hours > 0) parts.push(`${hours} ${hours === 1 ? "hour" : "hours"}`);
529	  if (minutes > 0) parts.push(`${minutes} ${minutes === 1 ? "minute" : "minutes"}`);
530	  if (seconds > 0 || parts.length === 0) parts.push(`${seconds} ${seconds === 1 ? "second" : "seconds"}`);
531	  return parts.join(" ");
532	}
533	
534	function countBlockToolCalls(block: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[]): number {
535	  let count = 0;
536	  for (const item of block) {
537	    if (item.kind === "tool") count += 1;
538	    else if (item.kind === "tool_group") count += item.counts.total;
539	  }
540	  return count;
541	}
542	
543	function summarizeWorkIntervals(items: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[]): TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[] {
544	  const result: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[] = [];
545	  let workBlock: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder[] = [];
546	
547	  const flushWorkBlock = (nextItem: TerminalActivityItemWithOrder | null) => {
548	    if (workBlock.length === 0) {
549	      return;
550	    }
551	    const followedByMessage = nextItem?.kind === "message";
552	    const toolCallCount = countBlockToolCalls(workBlock);
553	    const shouldSummarize = followedByMessage && toolCallCount > 1;
554	
555	    if (!shouldSummarize) {
556	      result.push(...workBlock);
557	      workBlock = [];
558	      return;
559	    }
560	
561	    const firstItem = workBlock[0]!;
562	    const lastItem = workBlock[workBlock.length - 1]!;
563	    const firstTs = Date.parse(firstItem.timestamp);
564	    const endTs = nextItem ? Date.parse(nextItem.timestamp) : null;
565	    const lastTs = Date.parse(lastItem.timestamp);
566	    const durationMs = Number.isFinite(firstTs) && endTs != null && Number.isFinite(endTs)
567	      ? Math.max(0, endTs - firstTs)
568	      : (Number.isFinite(firstTs) && Number.isFinite(lastTs) ? Math.max(0, lastTs - firstTs) : 0);
569	    const inProgress = workBlock.some((item) => {
570	      if (item.kind === "thinking") return item.inProgress;
571	      if (item.kind === "tool" || item.kind === "tool_group") return isRunningActivityStatus(item.status);
572	      return false;
573	    });
574	    result.push({
575	      id: `work-summary:${firstItem.id}`,
576	      kind: "work_summary",
577	      durationMs,
578	      timestamp: firstItem.timestamp,
579	      inProgress,
580	      items: workBlock as AgentActivityItem[],
581	      streamSeq: firstItem.streamSeq,
582	    });
583	    workBlock = [];
584	  };
585	
586	  for (const item of items) {
587	    if (item.kind === "thinking" || item.kind === "tool" || item.kind === "tool_group" || item.kind === "permission") {
588	      workBlock.push(item);
589	    } else {
590	      flushWorkBlock(item);
591	      result.push(item);
592	    }
593	  }
594	  flushWorkBlock(null);
595	  return result;
596	}

679	function TimelineMarker({
680	  running = false,
681	  tone,
682	  variant,
683	}: {
684	  running?: boolean;
685	  tone: "thought" | "tool" | "error" | "user" | "permission";
686	  variant: "terminal" | "native";
687	}) {
688	  const toneClass = {
689	    thought: variant === "native"
690	      ? "border-muted-foreground/55 bg-muted-foreground/75"
691	      : "border-muted-foreground/55 bg-muted-foreground/75 dark:border-zinc-400/60 dark:bg-zinc-400/80",
692	    tool: variant === "native"
693	      ? "border-emerald-500/75 bg-emerald-500"
694	      : "border-emerald-500/75 bg-emerald-500 dark:border-emerald-400/75 dark:bg-emerald-400",
695	    error: variant === "native"
696	      ? "border-destructive/80 bg-destructive"
697	      : "border-red-500/80 bg-red-500 dark:border-red-400/80 dark:bg-red-400",

813	type DiffDisplayRow = {
814	  id: string;
815	  kind: "context" | "add" | "remove" | "separator";
816	  visible: string;
817	  lineNumber: number | null;
818	};
819	
820	type ParsedDiffPane = {
821	  fileName: string | null;
822	  added: number;
823	  removed: number;
824	  rows: DiffDisplayRow[];
825	};
826	
827	function basenameDiffPath(value: string): string {
828	  const trimmed = value.trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
829	  const cleaned = trimmed.replace(/^(?:a|b)\//, "");
830	  const segments = cleaned.split(/[/\\]/).filter(Boolean);
831	  return segments[segments.length - 1] || cleaned || trimmed;
832	}
833	
834	function extractDiffFileName(line: string): string | null {
835	  if (line.startsWith("diff --")) {
836	    const parts = line.trim().split(/\s+/);
837	    return basenameDiffPath(parts[parts.length - 1] ?? "");
838	  }
839	
840	  if (line.startsWith("*** Update File:") || line.startsWith("*** Add File:") || line.startsWith("*** Delete File:")) {
841	    return basenameDiffPath(line.slice(line.indexOf(":") + 1));
842	  }
843	
844	  if (line.startsWith("+++ ") && !line.startsWith("+++ /dev/null")) {
845	    return basenameDiffPath(line.slice(4));
846	  }
847	
848	  if (line.startsWith("--- ") && !line.startsWith("--- /dev/null")) {
849	    return basenameDiffPath(line.slice(4));
850	  }
851	
852	  return null;
853	}
854	
855	function parseHunkStart(line: string): { oldLine: number; newLine: number } | null {
856	  const match = line.match(/^@@\s+-(\d+)(?:,\d+)?\s+\+(\d+)(?:,\d+)?/);
857	  if (!match) {
858	    return null;
859	  }
860	
861	  return {
862	    oldLine: Number(match[1]),
863	    newLine: Number(match[2]),
864	  };
865	}
866	
867	function isDiffMetadataLine(line: string): boolean {
868	  return line.startsWith("diff --")
869	    || line.startsWith("+++")
870	    || line.startsWith("---")
871	    || line.startsWith("***")
872	    || line.startsWith("index ")
873	    || line.startsWith("\\ No newline");
874	}
875	
876	function parseDiffPane(text: string): ParsedDiffPane {
877	  const rows: DiffDisplayRow[] = [];
878	  let fileName: string | null = null;
879	  let oldLine: number | null = null;
880	  let newLine: number | null = null;
881	  let added = 0;
882	  let removed = 0;
883	  let pendingSeparator = false;
884	
885	  const addSeparator = (id: string) => {
886	    if (rows.length > 0 && rows[rows.length - 1]?.kind !== "separator") {
887	      rows.push({ id, kind: "separator", visible: "", lineNumber: null });
888	    }
889	  };
890	
891	  text.split("\n").forEach((line, index) => {
892	    fileName = fileName || extractDiffFileName(line);
893	
894	    if (/^\[\d+ unchanged lines omitted\]$/.test(line.trim())) {
895	      addSeparator(`${index}:omitted`);
896	      return;
897	    }
898	
899	    const hunkStart = parseHunkStart(line);
900	    if (hunkStart) {
901	      oldLine = hunkStart.oldLine;
902	      newLine = hunkStart.newLine;
903	      pendingSeparator = rows.length > 0;
904	      return;
905	    }
906	
907	    if (isDiffMetadataLine(line)) {
908	      return;
909	    }
910	
911	    if (pendingSeparator) {
912	      addSeparator(`${index}:hunk`);
913	      pendingSeparator = false;
914	    }
915	
916	    if (line.startsWith("+")) {
917	      rows.push({
918	        id: `${index}:add:${line}`,
919	        kind: "add",
920	        visible: line.slice(1),
921	        lineNumber: newLine,
922	      });
923	      added += 1;
924	      newLine = newLine == null ? null : newLine + 1;
925	      return;
926	    }
927	
928	    if (line.startsWith("-")) {
929	      rows.push({
930	        id: `${index}:remove:${line}`,
931	        kind: "remove",
932	        visible: line.slice(1),
933	        lineNumber: oldLine,
934	      });
935	      removed += 1;
936	      oldLine = oldLine == null ? null : oldLine + 1;
937	      return;
938	    }
939	
940	    const visible = line.startsWith(" ") ? line.slice(1) : line;
941	    rows.push({
942	      id: `${index}:context:${line}`,
943	      kind: "context",
944	      visible,
945	      lineNumber: newLine ?? oldLine,
946	    });
947	    oldLine = oldLine == null ? null : oldLine + 1;
948	    newLine = newLine == null ? null : newLine + 1;
949	  });
950	
951	  return { fileName, added, removed, rows };
952	}
953	
954	function diffRowClass(kind: DiffDisplayRow["kind"], variant: "terminal" | "native") {
955	  if (kind === "add") {
956	    return variant === "native"
957	      ? "bg-emerald-500/13 text-emerald-900 dark:text-emerald-200"
958	      : "bg-emerald-500/14 text-emerald-900 dark:bg-emerald-400/12 dark:text-emerald-100";
959	  }
960	  if (kind === "remove") {
961	    return variant === "native"
962	      ? "bg-red-500/13 text-red-900 dark:text-red-200"
963	      : "bg-red-500/14 text-red-900 dark:bg-red-400/12 dark:text-red-100";
964	  }
965	  if (kind === "separator") {
966	    return variant === "native"
967	      ? "bg-muted/45 text-muted-foreground"
968	      : "bg-muted/35 text-muted-foreground dark:bg-white/7 dark:text-zinc-500";
969	  }
970	  return variant === "native" ? "text-foreground" : "text-foreground dark:text-zinc-200";
971	}
972	
973	function diffLineNumberClass(kind: DiffDisplayRow["kind"], variant: "terminal" | "native") {
974	  if (kind === "add") {
975	    return variant === "native"
976	      ? "text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-300"
977	      : "text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-300";
978	  }
979	  if (kind === "remove") {
980	    return variant === "native"
981	      ? "text-red-700 dark:text-red-300"
982	      : "text-red-700 dark:text-red-300";
983	  }
984	  return variant === "native"
985	    ? "text-muted-foreground"
986	    : "text-muted-foreground dark:text-zinc-500";
987	}
988	
989	function diffChangeRailClass(kind: DiffDisplayRow["kind"], variant: "terminal" | "native") {

991	    return variant === "native" ? "bg-emerald-500" : "bg-emerald-400";

995	  }

997	}

1211	const PROJECT_FILE_REFERENCE_TOKEN_PATTERN = /(https?:\/\/[^\s<>()]+|\/[A-Za-z0-9._~/%+-][^\s<>()]*:\d+(?::\d+)?)/g;
1212	
1213	function ProjectFileReferenceText({
1214	  text,
1215	  projectRoot,
1216	  onOpenProjectFile,
1217	}: {
1218	  text: string;
1219	  projectRoot?: string | null;
1220	  onOpenProjectFile?: (file: ProjectFileReference) => void;
1221	}) {
1222	  if (!projectRoot || !onOpenProjectFile) {
1223	    return text;
1224	  }
1225	
1226	  const nodes: ReactNode[] = [];
1227	  let lastIndex = 0;
1228	  let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
1229	
1230	  PROJECT_FILE_REFERENCE_TOKEN_PATTERN.lastIndex = 0;
1231	  while ((match = PROJECT_FILE_REFERENCE_TOKEN_PATTERN.exec(text))) {
1232	    const token = [REDACTED]
1233	    const reference = parseProjectFileReference(token, projectRoot);
1234	    if (!reference) {
1235	      continue;
1236	    }
1237	
1238	    if (match.index > lastIndex) {
1239	      nodes.push(text.slice(lastIndex, match.index));
1240	    }
1241	
1242	    nodes.push(
1243	      <ProjectFileContextMenu
1244	        key={`${match.index}:${token}`}
1245	        reference={reference}
1246	        onOpen={onOpenProjectFile}
1247	      >
```

```text
112	  if (!text || !onOpenWorker || workers.length === 0) {

115	  const workerByNumber = new Map<number, ConversationWorkerRecord>();
116	  for (const worker of workers) {
117	    if (typeof worker.workerNumber === "number") {

119	    }

121	  if (workerByNumber.size === 0) {
122	    return text;

125	  let cursor = 0;
126	  let keyCounter = 0;

129	    const number = Number.parseInt(match[1]!, 10);
130	    const target = Number.isFinite(number) ? workerByNumber.get(number) : null;
131	    if (!target) {
132	      continue;
133	    }
134	    if (matchStart > cursor) {
135	      nodes.push(text.slice(cursor, matchStart));
136	    }
137	    const workerId = target.id;
138	    nodes.push(

145	        }}
146	        className="omni-worker-mention-link inline cursor-pointer underline decoration-dotted underline-offset-2 hover:text-foreground"
147	      >

149	      </button>,
150	    );
151	    cursor = matchStart + match[0].length;
152	  }
153	  if (cursor === 0) {
154	    return text;
155	  }
156	  if (cursor < text.length) {
157	    nodes.push(text.slice(cursor));
158	  }
159	  return nodes;
160	}

418	function renderSupervisorActivityIcon(item: Extract<ConversationTimelineItem, { type: "activity" }>) {
419	  const eventType = item.event?.eventType;
420	  const text = item.text.trim();
421	
422	  if (eventType === "worker_spawned" || item.id.startsWith("worker-start:") || text.startsWith("Starting worker ") || text.startsWith("Starting planning agent")) {
423	    return <CirclePlay className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />;

425	
426	  if (

429	    || eventType === "worker_stop_requested"
430	    || text.startsWith("Cancelled worker ")
431	    || text.startsWith("Stopped worker ")
432	    || text.startsWith("Stopping worker ")

436	
437	  if (

439	    || text.startsWith("Steering worker ")
440	    || text.startsWith("Waiting to steer worker ")
441	  ) {

449	  ) {

487	  onCopy?: (content: string, messageId: string) => void | Promise<void>;
488	}) {
489	  const { fullOutputOpenByMessageId } = useManagerSnapshot(conversationMainManager);
490	  const fullOutputOpen = Boolean(fullOutputOpenByMessageId[message.id]);
491	  const inferredWorkerId = inferWorkerIdFromMessage(message);
492	  const summaryText = extractLatestPlainTextTurn({
493	    outputEntries: agent?.outputEntries,
494	    currentText: agent?.currentText,
495	    lastText: agent?.lastText || message.content,
496	  }) || message.content.trim();
497	  const fullOutputAgent = agent ?? {
498	    name: inferredWorkerId ?? "worker",
499	    state: "done",
500	    currentText: "",
501	    lastText: message.content,
502	  };
503	
504	  return (
505	    <Collapsible open={fullOutputOpen} onOpenChange={(open) => conversationMainManager.setFullOutputOpen(message.id, open)}>
506	      <div className="omni-worker-output group/worker-output-actions overflow-hidden rounded-lg">
507	        <div className="space-y-3 p-4">
508	          <MarkdownContent
509	            content={summaryText}
510	            className="text-foreground"
511	            projectRoot={projectRoot}
512	            onOpenProjectFile={onOpenProjectFile}
513	          />
514	          {summaryText.trim() && onCopy ? (
515	            <WorkerOutputCopyAction
516	              messageId={message.id}
517	              content={summaryText}
518	              onCopy={onCopy}
519	            />
520	          ) : null}
521	          <CollapsibleTrigger
522	            className="omni-worker-output-toggle inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md text-xs font-medium transition-colors hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
523	            aria-label={fullOutputOpen ? "Hide full worker output" : "Show full worker output"}
524	          >
525	            <ChevronDown className={cn("h-3.5 w-3.5 transition-transform", fullOutputOpen && "rotate-180")} />
526	            {fullOutputOpen ? "Hide full output" : "Show full output"}
527	          </CollapsibleTrigger>
528	        </div>
529	        <CollapsibleContent>
530	          <div className="border-t border-border/35 bg-muted/20 p-2 dark:bg-background/70">
531	            <Terminal
532	              agent={fullOutputAgent}
533	              className="h-72"
534	              projectRoot={projectRoot}
535	              onOpenProjectFile={onOpenProjectFile}
536	              scrollAnchorKey={message.id}
537	            />
538	          </div>
539	        </CollapsibleContent>
540	      </div>
541	    </Collapsible>
542	  );
543	}

694	function FailoverChip({ events }: { events: ExecutionEventRecord[] }) {
695	  for (let i = events.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
696	    const event = events[i]!;
697	    if (event.eventType !== "worker_failover_completed") continue;
698	    let outgoingType: string | null = null;
699	    let newType: string | null = null;
700	    try {
701	      const details = event.details ? JSON.parse(event.details) : null;
702	      if (details && typeof details === "object") {
703	        const record = details as Record<string, unknown>;
704	        outgoingType = typeof record.outgoingType === "string" ? record.outgoingType : null;
705	        newType = typeof record.newType === "string" ? record.newType : null;
706	      }
707	    } catch {
708	      outgoingType = null;
709	      newType = null;
710	    }
711	    if (!outgoingType || !newType) return null;
712	    const outgoingLabel = WORKER_TYPE_LABELS[outgoingType as SupportedWorkerType] ?? outgoingType;
713	    const newLabel = WORKER_TYPE_LABELS[newType as SupportedWorkerType] ?? newType;
714	    return (
715	      <div className="flex">
716	        <span
717	          className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full border border-amber-200/40 bg-amber-100/30 px-3 py-1 text-xs text-amber-900 dark:border-amber-900/40 dark:bg-amber-950/30 dark:text-amber-200"
718	          aria-label={t("conversation.chip.switchedWorkersAria")}
719	        >
720	          <ArrowLeftRight className="h-3 w-3" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />
721	          {t("conversation.chip.switchedWorkers", { outgoing: outgoingLabel, incoming: newLabel })}
722	        </span>
723	      </div>
724	    );
725	  }
726	  return null;
727	}

777	export function ConversationMain({
778	  scrollRef,
779	  selectedRunId,
780	  selectedRun,
781	  welcomeRepoName,
782	  isDirectConversation,
783	  isPlanningConversation,
784	  isImplementationConversation,
785	  appErrors,
786	  conversationFailure,
787	  directConversationMessages,
788	  locallySentUserMessageIds,
789	  sendingUserMessageIds,
790	  expandedDirectMessageIds,
791	  toggleDirectMessageExpansion,
792	  primaryConversationAgent,
793	  primaryConversationWorkerId,
794	  initialWorkerEntries = {},
795	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
796	  isHydratingConversations,
797	  isSelectedConversationPreviewAvailable,
798	  isSelectedConversationLoaded,
799	  promotePlanningConversation,
800	  onStartReview,
801	  reviewRuns = [],
802	  reviewRounds = [],
803	  reviewFindings = [],
804	  conversationTimelineItems,
805	  recoverRun,
806	  recoveryState,
807	  recoveryIncidents,
808	  resumeRunRecovery,
809	  stopRunRecovery,
810	  showRecoverableRunningState,
811	  hasStuckWorker,
812	  latestUserCheckpoint,
813	  handleRetryMessage,
814	  handleResumeRunRecovery,
815	  handleStopRecoveryWait,
816	  handleStartEditingMessage,
817	  handleForkMessage,
818	  handleForkMessageIntoWorktree,
819	  handleConfirmForkMessageIntoWorktree,
820	  editingMessageId,
821	  editingMessageValue,
822	  setEditingMessageValue,
823	  handleCancelEditingMessage,
824	  handleSaveEditedMessage,
825	  handlePreflightConfirmationAnswer,
826	  isPreflightConfirmationAnswering,
827	  conversationAgents,
828	  showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
829	  directControlPendingAssistantStatus,
830	  showConversationExecution,
831	  liveExecutionStatus,
832	  liveThoughts,
833	  executionEvents,
834	  activeWorkers,
835	  emptyComposer,
836	  projectRoot,
837	  onOpenProjectFile,
838	  onOpenWorkerActivity,
839	  onRespondElicitation,
840	  onRespondPermission,
841	  respondingElicitationRequestId = null,
842	  respondingPermissionRequestId = null,
843	}: ConversationMainProps) {
844	  useI18nSnapshot();
845	  const { hasOutputBelow } = useManagerSnapshot(conversationMainManager);
846	  const { handledMessageIds: handledPreflightConfirmationMessageIds } = useManagerSnapshot(preflightConfirmationActionsManager);
847	  const selectedRunIsTerminal = isTerminalRunStatus(selectedRun?.status);
848	  // Subscribe to the unified worker conversation stream for the
849	  // direct-control worker. When the flag is enabled this drives the
850	  // Terminal directly; otherwise the legacy `agent` + `userMessages`
851	  // path renders. `null` workerId returns an empty state and skips
852	  // the fetch.
853	  const directWorkerStream = useWorkerStream(
854	    unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled ? primaryConversationWorkerId : null,
855	    primaryConversationWorkerId ? initialWorkerEntries[primaryConversationWorkerId] ?? [] : [],
856	    {
857	      refreshIntervalMs: resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval({
858	        unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
859	        primaryConversationWorkerId,
860	        activeRefreshIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,
861	        validationIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS,
862	        showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
863	        selectedRunIsTerminal,
864	      }),
865	    },
866	  );
867	  // The single-worker stream above is only the *active* worker's
868	  // transcript. When a run has cycled through multiple workers
869	  // (cancel → respawn) we also fetch the merged conversation
870	  // transcript so prior workers' content stays visible. The merged
871	  // stream is preferred when available; we fall back to the active
872	  // worker stream during the brief moment before the transcript hook
873	  // produces its first response.
874	  const conversationTranscript = useConversationTranscript(
875	    unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled ? selectedRunId : null,
876	    {
877	      enabled: unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled && Boolean(selectedRunId),
878	      refreshIntervalMs: resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval({
879	        unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
880	        primaryConversationWorkerId,
881	        activeRefreshIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,
882	        validationIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS,
883	        showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
884	        selectedRunIsTerminal,
885	      }),
886	    },
887	  );
888	  // The run's worker list, not the entries loaded so far, decides how the
889	  // conversation is ordered — otherwise the rule flips from seq to timestamp
890	  // the moment the first transcript page arrives and the list re-sorts under
891	  // the reader. Undefined until the transcript answers, which leaves the
892	  // Terminal on its own inference for that first paint.
893	  const conversationRanOnMultipleWorkers = conversationTranscript.workerIds.length > 0
894	    ? conversationTranscript.workerIds.length > 1
895	    : undefined;
896	  // The server re-parses `supersededSeqRanges` into a fresh array on every
897	  // snapshot, so depending on it by identity would invalidate the merge below
898	  // on every frame even though its contents almost never change. The list is
899	  // tiny (usually empty), so round-tripping it is far cheaper than the rebuild
900	  // it prevents.
901	  const supersededSeqRangesKey = JSON.stringify(primaryConversationAgent?.supersededSeqRanges ?? []);
902	  const supersededSeqRanges = useMemo(
903	    () => JSON.parse(supersededSeqRangesKey) as SupersededSeqRange[],
904	    [supersededSeqRangesKey],
905	  );
906	  // Memoized because this array is the `entries` prop Terminal keys its
907	  // activity derivation on. Rebuilding it every render handed Terminal a new
908	  // reference each time, so the activity rebuild — measured at ~3ms for a
909	  // 2k-entry conversation, and several times that on a phone — re-ran on every
910	  // SSE frame while an agent was streaming, for an identical result.
911	  const conversationEntries = useMemo(
912	    () => selectDirectConversationEntries({
913	      transcriptEntries: conversationTranscript.entries,
914	      directWorkerEntries: directWorkerStream.entries,
915	      supersededSeqRanges,
916	      workerOrder: conversationTranscript.workerIds,
917	    }),
918	    [
919	      conversationTranscript.entries,
920	      conversationTranscript.workerIds,
921	      directWorkerStream.entries,
922	      supersededSeqRanges,
923	    ],
924	  );
925	  // Only the runtime owns a promise that can consume an answer. Stream rows
926	  // are durable history and may outlive that promise across a runner crash;
927	  // rendering them as forms makes a dead question look actionable.
928	  const pendingElicitations = primaryConversationAgent?.pendingElicitations ?? [];
929	  // Gated here rather than upstream because this is the only place that knows
930	  // what the prompt cards below the Terminal are actually rendering: the
931	  // elicitation card also draws on `directWorkerStream.entries`, which the
932	  // upstream resolver never sees. Note the refresh-interval calls above
933	  // deliberately keep using the ungated prop — polling cadence should follow
934	  // "is the worker busy", not "is a card on screen".
935	  const showPendingAssistantIndicator = shouldShowDirectControlWorkingIndicator({
936	    pendingAssistantVisible: showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
937	    primaryConversationWorkerId,
938	    renderedElicitationCount: pendingElicitations.length,
939	    renderedPermissionCount: primaryConversationAgent?.pendingPermissions?.length ?? 0,
940	  });
941	  const isUsingConversationTranscriptEntries = conversationTranscript.entries.length > 0;
942	  // Latched (`hasEverLoaded` / `hasLoadedOnce`), not momentary (`isLoaded`):
943	  // isLoaded flips false on every appended entry and every 2s transcript
944	  // poll, and each flip removed fallback-rendered user bubbles from the
945	  // transcript — the just-sent message visibly blinked in and out until its
946	  // stream entry arrived. The gate only exists to keep stale historical
947	  // rows from rendering before the stream's *first* load.
948	  const allowDirectUserMessageFallback = Boolean(
949	    !unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled
950	      || directWorkerStream.hasEverLoaded
951	      || conversationTranscript.hasLoadedOnce,
952	  );
953	  const directConversationLoadState = deriveConversationLoadState({
954	    snapshotLoaded: isSelectedConversationPreviewAvailable,
955	    unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
956	    primaryConversationWorkerId,
957	    streamState: directWorkerStream.state,
958	    selectedRunIsTerminal,
959	  });
960	  const isDirectWorkerStreamLoading = shouldShowDirectConversationLoading(directConversationLoadState)
961	    || Boolean(
962	      selectedRun
963	      && !isTerminalRunStatus(selectedRun.status)
964	      && directConversationMessages.length === 0
965	      && (!directWorkerStream.entries || directWorkerStream.entries.length === 0)
966	    );
967	  const forkWorkspaceSelector = useMemo(() => {
968	    return (state: ReturnType<typeof gitWorkspaceManager.getSnapshot>) => {
969	      const dialog = state.activeDialog?.kind === "fork_message_worktree" || state.activeDialog?.kind === "fork_session_worktree"
970	        ? state.activeDialog
971	        : null;
972	      const projectPath = dialog?.projectPath ?? null;
973	      return {
974	        dialog,
975	        snapshot: projectPath ? state.snapshotsByProject[projectPath] : undefined,
976	        loading: projectPath ? Boolean(state.loadingByProject[projectPath]) : false,
977	        pendingOperation: state.pendingOperation,
978	        dialogDraft: state.dialogDraft,
979	        lastError: projectPath ? state.lastErrorByProject[projectPath] ?? null : null,
980	      };
981	    };
982	  }, []);
983	  const { dialog: forkWorkspaceDialog, snapshot: forkWorkspaceSnapshot, loading: forkWorkspaceLoading, pendingOperation: forkWorkspacePendingOperation, dialogDraft: forkWorkspaceDraft, lastError: forkWorkspaceError } = useManagerSelector(
984	    gitWorkspaceManager,
985	    forkWorkspaceSelector,
986	    shallowEqualRecord,
987	  );
988	  const forkBranchName = forkWorkspaceDraft.branchName;
989	  const forkCheckoutPath = forkWorkspaceDraft.checkoutPath;
990	  useEffect(() => {
991	    if (!forkWorkspaceDialog) {
992	      return;
993	    }
994	    void gitWorkspaceManager.loadStatus(forkWorkspaceDialog.projectPath).catch(() => undefined);
995	  }, [forkWorkspaceDialog]);
996	  useEffect(() => {
997	    if (!forkWorkspaceDialog || !forkWorkspaceSnapshot) {
998	      return;
999	    }
1000	    const nextBranch = `fork/${slugBranchName(selectedRun?.title || forkWorkspaceSnapshot.branchName || forkWorkspaceSnapshot.detachedLabel || "workspace")}`;
1001	    gitWorkspaceManager.setDialogDraft({
1002	      branchName: nextBranch,
1003	      checkoutPath: suggestCheckoutPath(forkWorkspaceSnapshot.repoRoot, nextBranch),
1004	    });
1005	  }, [forkWorkspaceDialog, forkWorkspaceSnapshot, selectedRun?.title]);
1006	  const handleCopyDirectMessage = async (content: string, messageId: string) => {
1007	    try {
1008	      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(content);
1009	      conversationCopyNoticeManager.showCopiedMessage(messageId);
1010	    } catch (error) {
1011	      console.error("Copy message failed:", error);
1012	    }
1013	  };
1014	  const canRetryConversation = isDirectConversation || (isImplementationConversation && selectedRun?.status !== "failed");
1015	  const canRecoverUserMessage = isDirectConversation || isImplementationConversation;
1016	  const getUserMessageActions = (message: Pick<MessageRecord, "id" | "content">): UserInputMessageAction[] => {
1017	    if (!canRecoverUserMessage) {
1018	      return [];
1019	    }
1020	
1021	    const copyAction: UserInputMessageAction = {
1022	      label: t("conversation.message.copyAria"),
1023	      title: t("conversation.message.copyAria"),
1024	      icon: <Copy className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />,
1025	      onClick: () => void handleCopyDirectMessage(message.content, message.id),
1026	      feedback: "copy-message",

1028	
1029	    const retryActions: UserInputMessageAction[] = [
1030	      {
1031	        label: t(isImplementationConversation ? "conversation.message.action.resumeFromHere" : "conversation.message.action.retryFromHere"),
1032	        icon: <RotateCcw className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />,
1033	        disabled: recoverRun.isPending,
1034	        onClick: () => handleRetryMessage(message.id),
1035	      },
1036	    ];
1037	
1038	    if (!isDirectConversation) {
1039	      return retryActions;
1040	    }
1041	
1042	    return [
1043	      copyAction,
1044	      ...retryActions,
1045	      {
1046	        label: t("conversation.message.action.editInPlace"),
1047	        icon: <Pencil className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />,
1048	        disabled: recoverRun.isPending,
```

```text
1	import { normalizeWorkerStatus } from "@/lib/conversation-workers";
2	import { isTerminalRunStatus } from "@/lib/run-status";
3	import type { AgentOutputEntry } from "@/lib/agent-output";
4	
5	const DIRECT_WORKING_STATUSES = new Set(["starting", "working", "stuck", "recovering"]);
6	const DIRECT_WAITING_RUN_STATUSES = new Set(["quota_waiting", "needs_recovery"]);
7	const TERMINAL_HUMAN_INPUT_STATUSES = new Set([
8	  "answered",
9	  "approved",
10	  "cancelled",
11	  "canceled",
12	  "completed",
13	  "declined",
14	  "denied",
15	  "failed",
16	  "rejected",
17	  "skipped",
18	]);
19	
20	export type DirectControlPendingAssistantStatus = "connecting" | "thinking" | "working";
21	
22	function hasWorkingStatus(statuses: readonly (string | null | undefined)[]) {
23	  return statuses.some((status) => DIRECT_WORKING_STATUSES.has(normalizeWorkerStatus(status)));
24	}
25	
26	function isOpenInputEntry(entry: AgentOutputEntry) {
27	  if (entry.type !== "permission" && entry.type !== "elicitation") {
28	    return false;
29	  }
30	  const status = (entry.status ?? "pending").trim().toLowerCase();
31	  return !TERMINAL_HUMAN_INPUT_STATUSES.has(status);
32	}
33	
34	function entryRequestKey(entry: AgentOutputEntry) {
35	  const raw = entry.raw;
36	  if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null) {
37	    return null;
38	  }
39	  const requestId = (raw as { requestId?: unknown }).requestId;
40	  return typeof requestId === "number" && Number.isFinite(requestId)
41	    ? `${entry.type}:${requestId}`
42	    : null;
43	}
44	
45	export function countOpenHumanInputEntries(
46	  entries: readonly AgentOutputEntry[] | null | undefined,
47	  inputType?: "permission" | "elicitation",
48	) {
49	  const openByRequestKey = new Map<string, boolean>();
50	  let unkeyedOpenCount = 0;
51	
52	  for (const entry of entries ?? []) {
53	    if (entry.type !== "permission" && entry.type !== "elicitation") {
54	      continue;
55	    }
56	    if (inputType && entry.type !== inputType) {
57	      continue;
58	    }
59	
60	    const open = isOpenInputEntry(entry);
61	    const requestKey = entryRequestKey(entry);
62	    if (!requestKey) {
63	      if (open) {
64	        unkeyedOpenCount += 1;
65	      }
66	      continue;
67	    }
68	
69	    openByRequestKey.set(requestKey, open);
70	  }
71	
72	  return unkeyedOpenCount + [...openByRequestKey.values()].filter(Boolean).length;
73	}
74	
75	export function hasPendingHumanInputSignal(agent: {
76	  pendingPermissions?: unknown[] | null;
77	  pendingElicitations?: unknown[] | null;
78	  outputEntries?: AgentOutputEntry[] | null;
79	}) {
80	  return (
81	    (agent.pendingPermissions?.length ?? 0) > 0
82	    || (agent.pendingElicitations?.length ?? 0) > 0
83	    || countOpenHumanInputEntries(agent.outputEntries) > 0
84	  );
85	}
86	
87	export function resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus(args: {
88	  isDirectConversation: boolean;
89	  pendingConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
90	  busyConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
91	  selectedRunStatus: string | null | undefined;
92	  workerStatuses: readonly (string | null | undefined)[];
93	  agentStates: readonly (string | null | undefined)[];
94	  hasAgentCurrentText: boolean;
95	  hasPendingHumanInput?: boolean;
96	}) {
97	  if (!args.isDirectConversation) {
98	    return null;
99	  }
100	
101	  if (isTerminalRunStatus(args.selectedRunStatus)) {
102	    return null;
103	  }
104	
105	  if (DIRECT_WAITING_RUN_STATUSES.has((args.selectedRunStatus ?? "").trim().toLowerCase())) {
106	    return null;
107	  }
108	
109	  if (args.hasPendingHumanInput) {
110	    return null;
111	  }
112	
113	  if (args.busyConversationWorkerId || hasWorkingStatus(args.workerStatuses) || hasWorkingStatus(args.agentStates)) {
114	    return "working";
115	  }
116	
117	  if (args.hasAgentCurrentText) {
118	    return "thinking";
119	  }
120	
121	  if (args.pendingConversationWorkerId) {
122	    return "connecting";
123	  }
124	
125	  return null;
126	}
127	
128	export function shouldShowDirectControlPendingAssistant(args: Parameters<typeof resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus>[0]) {
129	  return resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus(args) !== null;
130	}
131	
132	/**
133	 * Final say on the "Working…" row, applied where the prompt cards actually
134	 * render. `resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus` suppresses the row via
135	 * `hasPendingHumanInput`, but it only sees the live agent snapshot, whereas the
136	 * elicitation card renders from a union of that snapshot and prompts derived
137	 * from the durable worker-entry stream. Any frame that lost the live pending
138	 * request — a degraded/persisted SSE frame, or a runtime fetch that raced the
139	 * poll — left the card on screen (worker entries still carry it) while the
140	 * indicator flipped back on, so "Working…" blinked in and out on every frame
141	 * and shoved the whole form down the page mid-answer.
142	 *
143	 * A rendered prompt means the turn is parked on the user, and the indicator is
144	 * a placeholder for assistant output that has not arrived yet, so the two can
145	 * never legitimately be true at once. Deciding that from the same counts that
146	 * gate the cards keeps them consistent no matter which source flickers.
147	 */
148	export function shouldShowDirectControlWorkingIndicator(args: {
149	  pendingAssistantVisible: boolean;
150	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
151	  renderedElicitationCount: number;
152	  renderedPermissionCount: number;
153	}) {
154	  if (!args.pendingAssistantVisible) {
155	    return false;
156	  }
157	
158	  const hasRenderedPrompt = Boolean(args.primaryConversationWorkerId)
159	    && (args.renderedElicitationCount > 0 || args.renderedPermissionCount > 0);
160	
161	  return !hasRenderedPrompt;
162	}
163	
164	export function isMutationPendingForSelectedRun(args: {
165	  isPending: boolean;
166	  mutationRunId: string | null | undefined;
167	  selectedRunId: string | null | undefined;
168	}) {
169	  return Boolean(
170	    args.isPending
171	      && args.selectedRunId
172	      && args.mutationRunId === args.selectedRunId,
173	  );
174	}
175	
176	export function resolvePendingConversationWorkerId(args: {
177	  isPending: boolean;
178	  mutationRunId: string | null | undefined;
179	  selectedRunId: string | null | undefined;
180	  isImplementationConversation: boolean;
181	  selectedWorkerIds: readonly string[];
182	}) {
183	  if (args.isImplementationConversation) {
184	    return null;
185	  }
186	
187	  if (!isMutationPendingForSelectedRun({
188	    isPending: args.isPending,
189	    mutationRunId: args.mutationRunId,
190	    selectedRunId: args.selectedRunId,
191	  })) {
192	    return null;
193	  }
194	
195	  return args.selectedWorkerIds[0] ?? null;
196	}
```

````text
function dedupeUserActivityByMessageId<T extends TerminalActivityItemWithOrder>(items: T[]): T[] {
  // Last occurrence wins: the entries feeding this list arrive oldest-first
  // (the transcript is sorted server-side), so the final copy of a message id
  // is its most recent delivery. `streamSeq` cannot break the tie — it is
  // per-worker, and the re-delivery starts a new worker's numbering.
  const lastIndexByMessageId = new Map<string, number>();
  items.forEach((item, index) => {
    if (item.kind === "user_message") {
      lastIndexByMessageId.set(item.messageId, index);
    }
  });

  return items.filter((item, index) => (
    item.kind !== "user_message" || lastIndexByMessageId.get(item.messageId) === index
  ));
}
```

}
````

````text
if (shouldSubmitComposerKeyDown({

})) {

  const useAlternateBusyAction = shouldUseAlternateComposerSubmitKeyDown({
    key: e.key,
    shiftKey: e.shiftKey,
    metaKey: e.metaKey,
    ctrlKey: e.ctrlKey,
    isApplePlatform: isAppleComposerShortcutPlatform(),
  });
  if (isStopButtonVisible) {

    }

  if (!isComposerSubmitting && (trimmedCommand || hasAttachments)) {
    if (selectedRunId && !hasAttachments && isManualStopCommand(command)) {
      setComposerDraft({ command: "", commandCursor: 0 });
      onStopConversation();
      return;
    }
    if (selectedRunId) {
      onSendConversationMessage(
        command,
        resolveBusyMessageActionForSubmitAction(composerBehavior.submitAction, {
          useAlternate: composerBehavior.allowAlternateBusyAction && useAlternateBusyAction,
        }),
      );
    } else {
      onRunCommand(command);
    }
  }
}

## 2. HANDLER CHAIN

## 3. OPTIMISTIC MESSAGE INSERTION

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeMutations.ts`** (lines 548-589)

The `sendConversationMessage` mutation's `onMutate` phase runs **synchronously before the POST request** and inserts an optimistic message:

```typescript
const sendConversationMessage = useMutation({
  // The user's bubble must exist continuously from the moment they hit
  // send: optimistic row now, swapped for the server's row on success,
  // removed (with the draft restored) on error. Appearing only on POST
  // success made the bubble pop in late and flicker.
  onMutate: (payload: {
    runId: string;
    content: string;
    attachments: PendingChatAttachment[];
    busyAction?: BusyMessageAction;
  }) => {
    const snapshot = homeUiStateManager.getSnapshot();
    const optimisticMessage = buildOptimisticSentConversationMessage({
      runId: payload.runId,
      content: payload.content,
      attachments: payload.attachments.map(({ id, kind, name, mimeType, size, previewUrl }) => (
        { id, kind, name, mimeType, size, previewUrl }
      )),
    });
    pendingSentConversationMessagesRef.current.set(optimisticMessage.id, optimisticMessage);
    locallySentMessageIdsRef.current.add(optimisticMessage.id);
    sendingMessageIdsRef.current.add(optimisticMessage.id);
    setState((current) => appendSentConversationMessageSnapshot(current, optimisticMessage));
    const ownsSideEffects = ownsConversationSideEffects({
      runId: payload.runId,
      currentSelectedRunId: snapshot.selectedRunId,
    });
    const composerCleared = ownsSideEffects && snapshot.command === payload.content;
    if (composerCleared) {
      setCommand("");
      clearAttachments();
    }
    if (ownsSideEffects) {
      scrollConversationToBottom();
    }
    return {
      commandAtStart: snapshot.command,
      attachmentsAtStart: snapshot.attachments,
      optimisticMessageId: optimisticMessage.id,
      composerCleared,
    };
  },
```

### Optimistic Message Shape & ID

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/utils.ts`** (lines 202-219)

```typescript
export function buildOptimisticSentConversationMessage(args: {
  runId: string;
  content: string;
  attachments?: ChatAttachment[];
}): MessageRecord {
  const id = typeof crypto !== "undefined" && "randomUUID" in crypto
    ? `optimistic-${crypto.randomUUID()}`
    : `optimistic-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(16).slice(2)}`;
  return {
    id,
    runId: args.runId,
    role: "user",
    kind: null,
    content: args.content,
    attachments: args.attachments ?? [],
    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  };
}
```

**Storage locations for optimistic message:**
- `pendingSentConversationMessagesRef.current.set(optimisticMessage.id, optimisticMessage)` — stored by optimistic ID
- `locallySentMessageIdsRef.current.add(optimisticMessage.id)` — tracked as locally sent
- `sendingMessageIdsRef.current.add(optimisticMessage.id)` — marked as in-flight
- Appended to `state.messages` via `appendSentConversationMessageSnapshot`

## 4. POST REQUEST & SUCCESS RECONCILIATION

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeMutations.ts`** (lines 590-663)

}) => {

    runId: payload.runId,
    body: {
      content: payload.content,
      attachments: uploadedAttachments,
      busyAction: payload.busyAction,

    },
  }) as Promise<{

}

On `onSuccess`, the reconciliation happens:

```typescript
onSuccess: (data, variables, context) => {
  if (context) {
    pendingSentConversationMessagesRef.current.delete(context.optimisticMessageId);
    locallySentMessageIdsRef.current.delete(context.optimisticMessageId);
    sendingMessageIdsRef.current.delete(context.optimisticMessageId);
  }
  if (data.message) {
    pendingSentConversationMessagesRef.current.set(data.message.id, data.message);
    locallySentMessageIdsRef.current.add(data.message.id);
  }
  if (data.queuedMessage) {
    if (variables.busyAction === "steer" && data.message) {
      busyMessageQueueManager.hideQueuedMessage(data.queuedMessage.id);
    } else {
      busyMessageQueueManager.upsertQueuedMessage(data.queuedMessage);
    }
  }
  setState((current) => (
    context
      ? resolveOptimisticSentConversationMessage(current, context.optimisticMessageId, data.message)
      : appendSentConversationMessageSnapshot(current, data.message)
  ));
  // ... handle side effects ...
}
```

### Reconciliation Key

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/utils.ts`** (lines 226-236)

The key used to match and replace is the **optimistic message ID**:

```typescript
export function resolveOptimisticSentConversationMessage(
  current: EventStreamState,
  optimisticMessageId: string,
  message: MessageRecord | null | undefined,
): EventStreamState {
  const messages = (current.messages || []).filter((existing) => existing.id !== optimisticMessageId);
  const next = messages.length === (current.messages || []).length
    ? current
    : { ...current, messages };
  return message ? appendSentConversationMessageSnapshot(next, message) : next;
}
```

This removes the optimistic message by its ID (`optimisticMessageId`) from `state.messages`, then appends the server's real message (with a different real ID).

update(action: EventStreamStateAction, options: { snapshotSource?: EventStreamSnapshotSource } = {}) {
  const incoming = typeof action === "function" ? action(this.state) : action;
  const snapshotSource = options.snapshotSource
    ?? incoming.snapshotSource
    ?? this.state.snapshotSource;
  const incomingWithRuns = mergeScopedRuns(this.state, incoming, {
    serverAuthoritative: snapshotSource === "server",
  });
  const incomingWithAgents = mergeDegradedAgentHumanInput(this.state, incomingWithRuns);
  const nextState = {
    ...mergeScopedMessages(this.state, incomingWithAgents),
    snapshotSource,
  };

  if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
    return this.state;
  }

  this.state = nextState;
  this.snapshotCache.rememberState(nextState, this.snapshotCacheScope);
  this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener(this.state));
  return this.state;
}
```

## 7. MESSAGE SNAPSHOT CLOBBER BEHAVIOR

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/EventStreamStateManager.ts`** (lines 145-173)

The `mergeScopedMessages` function is **additive by design**—it never clobbers local optimistic state with a full server snapshot:

```typescript
function mergeScopedMessages(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {
  const incomingMessages = incoming.messages ?? [];
  const incomingMessageIds = new Set(incomingMessages.map((message) => message.id));
  const completeMessageRunIds = new Set(
    incoming.messageScope?.complete ? incoming.messageScope.runIds : [],
  );
  const liveRunIds = new Set((incoming.runs ?? []).map((run) => run.id));
  const retainedCurrentMessages = (current.messages || []).filter((message) => (
    liveRunIds.has(message.runId)
    && !incomingMessageIds.has(message.id)
    && !completeMessageRunIds.has(message.runId)
  ));
  const mergedMessages = sortMessages([
    ...retainedCurrentMessages,
    ...incomingMessages,
  ]);

  if (
    mergedMessages.length === incomingMessages.length
    && mergedMessages.every((message, index) => message === incomingMessages[index])
  ) {
    return incoming;
  }

  return {
    ...incoming,
    messages: mergedMessages,
  };
}
```

**Key behavior:**
- Retains local messages that are NOT in the incoming snapshot (line 152-156)
- Only drops local messages if the server explicitly declares the run's message scope as `complete` (line 149)
- This means optimistic messages persist until explicitly removed OR the server declares a full message sync for that run

## 8. WORKER ENTRIES & "Working..." INDICATOR

**File: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts`** (lines 1-30)

Worker conversation content is managed **separately** from the global event stream:

```typescript
/**
 * Single source of truth for the unified worker conversation stream on
 * the frontend.
 *
 * Per (workerId) we hold a contiguous *window* [lowestSeq..latestContiguousSeq]:
 *   - entries: the contiguous window in seq order, never with gaps.
 *   - lowestSeq: the lowest seq currently in `entries` (0 if empty).
 *   - latestContiguousSeq: the highest seq we have proven contiguous
 *     from lowestSeq. Used as the cursor for forward refetch.
 *   - latestKnownSeq: the highest seq the server has told us exists.
 *     Updates immediately on a wake-up frame; the fetch fills the gap.
 *   - hasOlder: true if older entries exist on the server before
 *     lowestSeq. Set by initial tail-load and `loadOlder`.
 *   - status: "idle" → "loading" → "loaded"; "error" on a fetch failure.
 *
 * Initial load fetches the last N entries via `?limit=N`. Forward
 * extension uses `?afterSeq=latestContiguousSeq`. Backward hydration
 * uses `?beforeSeq=lowestSeq&limit=N` via `loadOlder`.
 *
 * SSE frames carry only `{ workerId, seq }` — the content is fetched
 * via the HTTP endpoint. The frame is a wake-up hint; we never trust
 * it as the entry payload.
 */
```

When the server echoes back the user message and the worker begins responding, it arrives as worker entries (via HTTP fetch on wake-up), NOT as supervisor messages. The "Working..." indicator is driven by the run's status and worker presence, not by message content.

| **Event stream snapshot** | SSE (streamed) | Via `updateFromServer` → `EventStreamStateManager.update` | Per-message/per-run | Additive merge (preserves local unacknowledged messages) |
| **Worker entries** | HTTP fetch on SSE wake-up hint | `WorkerEntriesManager` (separate from event stream) | `seq` (per-worker stream) | Contiguous window maintained; never clobbers local |
````

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T08:55:58.982Z

I'm tracing through the flicker issue now. The optimistic bubble gets added with a temporary ID, then when the server responds, that optimistic entry should be atomically replaced with the real one via `resolveOptimisticSentConversationMessage` — so there shouldn't be a visual flicker. But I'm noticing Terminal constructs `userMessages` from both the state and the `WorkerEntriesManager` entries, and the deduplication logic in `workerEntryMatchesUserMessage` is checking entry types to match them up.

The sequence is: optimistic message appears, the worker stream delivers a matching `user_input` entry, then on success the optimistic gets removed and the server message appended. The timestamps could differ slightly between client and server clocks, but that shouldn't cause issues since `sortMessages` handles the ordering. The real question is what's happening in `resolveOptimisticSentConversationMessage` when it filters out the optimistic message.

If `data.message` is undefined—which happens in the busy or queued path—the optimistic message vanishes with nothing replacing it, causing the bubble to disappear until the SSE stream delivers the actual message. That's likely the flicker. But the user reports it happening even on normal sends, so I should look at `mergeScopedMessages` in the EventStreamStateManager instead, which filters retained messages based on run IDs.

There's a race condition here: if an SSE frame arrives between the optimistic insert and the POST response with `messageScope.complete === true` for the selected run, the optimistic message gets dropped because it's not yet in the server's incoming message IDs, causing the bubble to vanish. Then `onSuccess` appends the server message and it reappears—exactly matching the "appearing and disappearing once" behavior the user described. This is likely because sending a message immediately triggers worker activity, which generates an SSE frame, making this race window probable.

The `pendingSentConversationMessagesRef` is supposed to guard against this, but I need to verify if it's actually being used in the merge logic.

For the "Working..." indicator dance: `resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus` returns "working" when the worker is busy, "connecting" when there's a pending worker ID, and null otherwise. Right after sending, none of those conditions are met yet, so the indicator is null. Then it flashes to "connecting" and "working" as the server acknowledges. Meanwhile, `shouldTerminalScrollToLatest` blocks scrolling for pending_assistant messages, so the user sees the message appear, the indicator flicker on and off as the status changes.

Now I need to trace through `useHomeMutations` to see how `pendingSentConversationMessagesRef` is actually used and how `filterEventStreamState` consumes it in HomeApp.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T08:56:40.892Z

So the logic hinges on whether the run is terminal or not. When it's not terminal—still running or idle—`shouldReviveRunForSentMessage` returns true, which means the guard doesn't evict and re-appends instead. But once the run reaches a terminal state like completed or awaiting_user, and the message timestamp is older than when the run updated, that's when eviction happens. The race condition emerges here because of the timing between message creation and run state transitions.

The message's `createdAt` comes from the client's clock, while `run.updatedAt` is from the server. In the typical scenario where you send a message right after the agent finishes—when the run is terminal—if your client clock lags even slightly behind the server's, the comparison fails and the message gets dropped from the guard map immediately. Then when `onSuccess` fires with the actual server message, it reappears. That's the flicker—the bubble vanishes and comes back. It's clock-skew dependent, which explains why it's intermittent and feels like a dance.

There's also a timing window where the server bumps `run.updatedAt` after receiving the POST but before the status flips to running. If an SSE frame arrives during that gap with an updated timestamp that's still after the optimistic message's creation time while the run is still terminal, it triggers an eviction. Once `pendingMessages.delete()` removes it from the map, it's gone permanently—it can't be re-injected on later frames. And `mergeScopedMessages` will drop it anyway whenever the incoming frame marks that run as complete, so the guard is the only thing protecting it, and the guard just deleted it.

The "Working..." indicator flickers because `resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus` returns null whenever the run status is terminal, the worker isn't in the busy list, there's no agent text, and no pending worker. Right after the POST sends, the run is still terminal from the previous turn, so the indicator is null. Then the POST lands, the run flips to running, the worker gets attached, and it shows "connecting" then "working"—but if SSE frames interleave awkwardly (run running but worker not yet attached, or worker status momentarily not "working" with no currentText), it goes null again, causing the blink. And since `shouldTerminalScrollToLatest` returns false for `pending_assistant` messages, the indicator appearing doesn't trigger a scroll, which ties back to the earlier issue.

There's also a second dance happening: the optimistic message uses `new Date().toISOString()` for its timestamp while `sortMessages` orders by createdAt, so clock skew can make the optimistic bubble sort into the wrong position above older messages, then jump when the server replaces it. I should double-check the logic in `isTerminalRunStatus` and `DIRECT_WAITING_RUN_STATUSES` to make sure I have the details right.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T08:57:13.360Z

Terminal statuses include done, failed, cancelled, promoting, and promoted. The typical flow is that when you send a follow-up message, the previous run has already reached "done" status. This triggers a timestamp comparison between when the message was created and when the run last updated, which works fine on local machines but introduces potential clock skew issues between client and server.

The real problem emerges in `mergeScopedMessages` — it filters retained messages based on whether their run ID exists in the incoming frame's live runs set. When the server sends a complete message scope for the selected conversation (the normal steady-state), every SSE frame ends up dropping the optimistic message from the current state, and the only mechanism that could re-add it gets blocked.

The ordering in `useHomeLifecycle` actually works in our favor: `mergePendingSentConversationMessages` injects the pending message into the incoming data before `mergeScopedMessages` processes it, so it survives the filter. But that survival hinges entirely on the eviction logic in `mergePendingSentConversationMessages` — specifically the timestamp check on line 257 that removes the message when the run is terminal and `messageCreatedAt` isn't greater than `runUpdatedAt`.

The real culprit is clock skew with remote runners. The runner's server clock sets `run.updatedAt`, while the browser sets `message.createdAt`. If the runner's clock is ahead by even a second and the run is already "done", then `messageCreatedAt > runUpdatedAt` fails and the message gets evicted — causing the flicker.

But I should also check the direct-control mode path. In that mode, Terminal builds user messages from worker stream entries, falling back to `userMessages`, and there's a matcher function that compares entries against messages by checking the entry type, ID, and normalized text content along with timestamp proximity.

Checking matcher logic...

The optimistic message gets a client-side `createdAt` timestamp while the worker entry has a runner timestamp. If they drift more than 5 seconds apart, the dedup fails and the message renders twice — once from the worker entry, once from the fallback. Within that window it dedupes correctly.

For the flicker itself, the sequence in direct mode is: optimistic message lands in state and renders via the fallback path (bubble appears), then on success the optimistic gets removed and the server message appends with a new ID, triggering a re-render with the same text still via fallback. Should stay continuous, but something's breaking that.

The real culprit is the React key changing — from `optimistic-uuid` to the server ID. That key swap unmounts and remounts the row, and any enter animation or transition on the bubble reads as a flash. Then the worker stream delivers a `user_input` entry, shifting the bubble to render from the entry instead of the fallback, which changes the key again and remounts it a second time. So the same visual bubble gets mounted under three different React keys in about a second, causing visible flicker and reflow. Combined with the scroll bug from earlier where each remount changes content height and triggers competing smooth scrolls, that's exactly the "dance" effect.

Now I need to check the `dedupeUserActivityByMessageId` function and how the activity is built to confirm this keying behavior.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T08:57:39.908Z

I'm tracing through the flicker sequence to understand how `ungatedUserMessageIds` maps to `locallySentMessageIdsRef.current`, checking the prop naming between HomeApp and Terminal to confirm the connection.

The core issue is React key identity driving the flicker: when the optimistic message (key `user:optimistic-<uuid>`) gets replaced by the server message (key `user:<serverId>`), React unmounts and remounts the row. Then when the worker stream delivers a `user_input` entry with the same id, the fallback filter drops the optimistic message and rebuilds from the stream entry instead—but if the runner assigns its own id, the key might shift again, causing another unmount/remount cycle.

Between the server response and the stream entry arriving, the row loses its `sending` state (opacity returns to full), gains action buttons, and its timestamp/sort position can change relative to the pending assistant item. The "Working..." indicator itself blinks because `pendingAssistantActivity` has a constant id but its timestamp shifts when `latestActivityTimestamp` recomputes—and the indicator's visibility is gated on `resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus`, which returns null in the gap between the previous run finishing and the worker reattaching, so both the pending row and the user message row churn through visibility and sort order changes simultaneously.

The actual disappearance bug happens in the eviction logic: when sending a follow-up into a completed run, the code compares the message's creation time (from browser clock) against the run's `updatedAt` (from server clock). If the server clock is ahead, the comparison fails and the pending message gets permanently deleted from the guard map before the stream entry can arrive to replace it.

I'll write this up as a diagnosis with a proposed fix and offer to implement it, keeping it straightforward this time.

## Claude · 2026-08-04T08:58:07.507Z

Different bug, and I found it. It's a clock comparison plus React key churn.

## The disappearance

`filterEventStreamState` (`HomeApp.tsx:430`) is what keeps the optimistic bubble alive across SSE frames, because `mergeScopedMessages` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:145`) drops any local message not in the incoming frame whenever the frame declares `messageScope.complete` for that run — which is the steady state for the selected conversation. The only thing re-injecting it is `mergePendingSentConversationMessages`. And that function evicts:

```ts
// utils.ts:256
const incomingRun = incomingRunsById.get(message.runId);
if (incomingRun && !shouldReviveRunForSentMessage(incomingRun, message)) {
  pendingMessages.delete(messageId);   // permanent — never retried
  continue;
}
```

`shouldReviveRunForSentMessage` (`utils.ts:170`) short-circuits to `true` only for non-terminal runs. But `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` is `done/failed/cancelled/promoting/promoted` (`run-status.ts:1`) — and `done` is precisely the state a conversation sits in when you type a follow-up. So it falls through to:

```ts
return messageCreatedAt > runUpdatedAt;
```

`messageCreatedAt` is the **browser** clock (`new Date().toISOString()`, `utils.ts:216`). `runUpdatedAt` is the **runner's** clock. Any skew where the runner is ahead makes this `false`, the pending message is `delete`d from the ref-held Map, and the next SSE frame drops the bubble from `state.messages`. It comes back when `onSuccess` appends the server row. One appear → disappear → reappear, exactly as you describe, and intermittent because it depends on skew and on whether a frame lands inside the POST window.

## The "dance"

Even when the row survives, it gets re-keyed twice. The activity id is `user:${messageId}` (`Terminal.tsx:2341`, `2379`):

1. `onMutate` → `user:optimistic-<uuid>`, rendered via the fallback path, `sending: true` → `opacity-70`
2. `onSuccess` → optimistic row removed, server row appended with a **new id** → `user:<serverId>`; React unmounts and remounts
3. worker stream delivers the `user_input` entry → the fallback filter at `Terminal.tsx:2323` now matches and drops it, so the row is rebuilt from the stream entry, gaining `streamSeq` and a different `timestamp`

Each step changes the key or the sort inputs, so the row remounts and can re-sort against the `pending-assistant` item — whose timestamp is `latestActivityTimestamp + 1` (`Terminal.tsx:2420`) and therefore *moves whenever the user row moves*. Meanwhile `resolveDirectControlPendingAssistantStatus` returns `null` while the run is still `done`, then `connecting`, then `working` — so "Working..." genuinely blinks off and on during the handoff.

One more: `sendingUserMessageIds` is `sendingMessageIdsRef.current` passed by reference (`HomeApp.tsx:1433`) and listed as a `useMemo` dep at `Terminal.tsx:2451`. Mutating the Set doesn't change the reference, so the memo never invalidates — the `opacity-70` clears late, on some unrelated re-render, which adds a second visible pop.

## Fix I'd apply

1. **Stop comparing clocks.** In `mergePendingSentConversationMessages`, never evict on the `shouldReviveRunForSentMessage` check — that predicate is for deciding whether to *revive* a run, not whether the user's own in-flight message is real. Evict only on `serverMessageIds.has(messageId)` (the line above it, which is correct) or on mutation settle.
2. **Stable identity across the swap.** Have the server echo back the client-generated id (send it in the POST body), or carry `optimisticId` on the server row and key the activity item off `optimisticId ?? id`. That collapses steps 1→2→3 into one continuously-mounted row.
3. **Anchor the pending-assistant item to the end of the list** rather than to `latestActivityTimestamp + 1`, so it can't swap places with the message that just arrived.
4. **Make `sendingUserMessageIds` state, not a mutable ref** (or pass a version counter alongside it) so the dimming clears on the same commit that clears the flag.

Fixes 1 and 4 are small and independent; 2 is the one that actually removes the remount churn and needs a server-side field.

I've stopped at diagnosis — say the word and I'll implement, either the whole set or just 1 and 4 as the low-risk pair.

Given that fixes 1, 3, and 4 are client-side and self-contained while fix 2 requires server changes, I'm leaning toward the broader interpretation. Though I'm also realizing the last message focused on bug #2 (the flicker issue), so there's some uncertainty about which problem we're actually addressing.

For fix #2, I could potentially solve it client-side by attaching the optimistic ID to the server message when they swap in `resolveOptimisticSentConversationMessage`—that way Terminal can key off the optimistic ID instead of the server ID. But this creates a problem at the third remount when the worker stream entry arrives, since it would have the server message ID and cause a key mismatch during the transition.

The cleaner approach is to make the server message ID the canonical key and have the optimistic row adopt it as soon as it's known. The real fix would be to send a client-generated ID in the POST request and have the server use it, but that requires server changes. Let me check if the sendTo endpoint already supports something like an idempotency key or client-supplied message ID.

I should start by reading the project conventions in agents.md and examining the server route, then implement the client-only fixes first and see if #2 is feasible without backend work.

```text
  const probe = startSlowProbe(`POST /api/conversations/${context.params?.id ?? "?"}/messages`);

    if (request.method !== "POST") {
      probe.end();
      return Response.json({ error: { code: "method_not_allowed", message: "Method not allowed." } }, {
        status: 405,
        headers: { allow: "POST" },
      });
    }

      source: "Conversations",
      action: "Send a conversation message",
      enforceSameOrigin: true,
    });
    probe.mark("auth");
    if (auth.response) {
      probe.end();
      return auth.response;
    }

    const runId = requireParam(context.params, "id");
    const body = await request.json();
    probe.mark("body");
    const content = String(body?.content ?? "").trim();
    const attachments = normalizeChatAttachments(body?.attachments);
    const busyAction = parseBusyMessageAction(body?.busyAction);
    const preferredWorkerType = typeof body?.preferredWorkerType === "string" ? body.preferredWorkerType : null;
    const preferredWorkerModel = typeof body?.preferredWorkerModel === "string" ? body.preferredWorkerModel : null;
    const preferredWorkerEffort = typeof body?.preferredWorkerEffort === "string" ? body.preferredWorkerEffort : null;
    const preferredWorkerAccountId = typeof body?.preferredWorkerAccountId === "string" ? body.preferredWorkerAccountId : null;
    const allowedWorkerTypes = Array.isArray(body?.allowedWorkerTypes) || typeof body?.allowedWorkerTypes === "string"
      ? body.allowedWorkerTypes
      : null;
    if (!content && attachments.length === 0) {
      return errorResponse("Message content or attachment is required", {
        status: 400,
        source: "Conversations",
        action: "Send a conversation message",
      });
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T08:58:56.138Z

There's an existing test that validates the eviction logic—it deliberately drops stale pending messages from previous sessions that are older than when the run completed, preventing them from resurrecting a finished run. So my fix needs to differentiate between genuinely stale messages versus ones that should be preserved.

The key insight is that the discriminator shouldn't be timestamp-based—it should be whether the send is still in flight. If the mutation hasn't settled yet, I should never evict. Once it resolves (success or error), the mutation handlers remove the entry anyway. So I'll add an explicit `inFlight` flag to pending entries, and `mergePendingSentConversationMessages` will skip the staleness eviction for in-flight ones. This preserves the existing test while fixing the bug.

But looking at the architecture guidelines, there are three separate refs tracking the same message lifecycle—`pendingSentConversationMessagesRef`, `locallySentMessageIdsRef`, and `sendingMessageIdsRef`—which violates the principle of centralizing state in a single manager class. I need to consolidate these into one unified data structure.

I'm thinking through a `SentConversationMessagesManager` that would track message state with phases like "sending" or "sent", expose derived views like pending messages and IDs, and provide methods for the full lifecycle. This would also fix the stale `sending` flag issue by letting components subscribe to state changes. But this is a significant refactor touching multiple files, so I need to be careful about scope and check how StateManager works first.

Looking at the four fixes the user approved, I realize fixes 1 and 4 both need the manager, while 2 and 3 are more targeted. For the stable React key across the optimistic-to-server swap, the cleanest approach is having the client generate the message ID upfront and having the server use it. Let me check the server's send-message function to see if that's feasible.
